newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania to trim banks ahead of sale.
newsitem.headline: Albania to trim banks ahead of sale.

text.p: Albania will streamline the activity of two of its state-owned banks, hiving off or shutting down unprofitable branches, to make them more attractive for sale, a government spokesman said on Tuesday.

Lorenc Ligori said the National Commercial Bank of Albania (NCBA) and the Rural Commercial Bank of Albania (RCBA) would transfer some of their branches to the Savings Bank, which will be privatised at a later stage.
"The decision aims at re-shaping the existing banking network by reducing or even shutting down unprofitable business to keep costs down," Ligori added.
He added the restructuring would take place in two stages. Initially the NCBA and RCBA would transfer a number of branches, agencies and offices to the Savings Bank.
Savings Bank foreign department chief Valer Miho said the Savings Bank would integrate the branches and agencies into its own activities, adapting them to its system.
"This might also lead to a restructuring of its own activity," Miho told Reuters. "In the second stage the Savings Bank will come up for sale itself," he added.
Albi Tola, NCBA's foreign department head, said both banks would be subject to a fresh audit after the transfer of activities.
"The government will be seeking strategic investors and will retain a share initially," Tola told Reuters. "By the end of 1998 it will leave the banks totally in private hands."
Albania created a two-tier banking system in 1992 with the Bank of Albania serving as a central institution to the state-owned NCBA, RCBA and the Savings Bank of Albania.
Bank of Albania has licensed two Greek banks and one Malaysian bank. The Greek banks have already opened branches in Tirana and the Malaysian bank is in the process of doing so.
NCBA is a partner of two banking joint-ventures, the Albanian-Italian Bank with Italy's Banca di Roma and the Arab Albanian Islamic Bank with Saudi and Bahreini investors.
The International Monetary Fund has repeatedly told Albania to accelerate the privatisation of its banks.
So-called pyramid schemes offering lucrative returns to depositors are taking huge sums of money away from formal banking channels.
